title: Bitcoin mining difficulty reaches new all-time high as hash
content:
TL;DR: The Bitcoin network continues its relentless operation, with current hashrate at 905.20 EH/s and a difficulty adjustment imminent in 339 blocks. While the difficulty remains below its November 2025 peak, the protocol's self-correcting mechanism is preparing for a likely downward adjustment, ensuring ongoing security and miner incentives. Transactors should monitor fee markets closely as network dynamics shift, reinforcing Bitcoin's incorruptible monetary policy in action.

The Report

As of February 05, 2026, at 07:03 UTC, the Bitcoin network stands robustly operational at block height 935,085. The global computational effort securing this decentralized monetary system is currently measured at a formidable 905.20 Exahashes per second (EH/s). This figure, while significant, marks a notable shift from the approximately 977 EH/s observed in late January, indicating a slight contraction in mining activity over the past two weeks. This dynamic underscores the highly competitive and incentive-driven nature of Bitcoin's proof-of-work mechanism.

The network is currently 83.2% through its 2,016-block difficulty epoch, with just 339 blocks remaining until the next automatic adjustment. Given the observed decrease in hashrate since the last adjustment, it is highly probable that the upcoming difficulty adjustment will be a downward revision. This self-regulating feature is a cornerstone of Bitcoin's design, ensuring that the average block time remains close to the target of ten minutes, regardless of fluctuations in mining power. Unlike fiat systems that rely on central bank mandates and arbitrary policy shifts, Bitcoin's monetary integrity is maintained by immutable code and economic incentives.

The current Bitcoin difficulty stands at 146.47 Trillion, a figure that, while immense, is important to note is NOT an all-time high. It remains below the peak of 155.9 Trillion recorded in November 2025. This distinction is crucial for understanding the network's long-term trajectory and avoiding sensationalized narratives. The system is designed to adapt, not merely to perpetually increase. Mining economics are constantly in flux, influenced by energy costs, hardware efficiency, and the Bitcoin price itself. A downward adjustment in difficulty would temporarily improve profit margins for less efficient miners or those operating with higher electricity costs, potentially re-attracting hashpower to the network.
